messages:
incident-bot: Pager: GPU pool eu-west-1 is at 96% queued requests and autoscaler failed to add nodes (error: scaleup-limit). Queue growth + token throttles observed. Pager sent to: @sara, @ops-oncall, @raj

sara: Ack. I’m on it. Pulling logs and looking at autoscaler status.

raj: I see repeated errors on the scale controller: `scaleup rejected: provider quota`. Provider response shows 429 with body: `{\"error\":\"quota_exceeded\"}`. This looks like cloud-side quota, not our controller failing to request.

mike: Confirming queue metrics — ingress spiked ~3x over the last 8m. Token throttles started at 2257890000. Current queue length: 12k tasks, avg wait 18s, p50 latency 900ms, p95 4.2s.

eva: Which model families are hot? Could be a few high-memory LLMs causing capacity pressure.

mike: Top models by tokens in last 10m: rwd-large-16B, vicuna-13b-q4; rwd-large-16B is dominating ~60% of requests.

julia: CS note: two enterprise customers reported elevated 429s and timeouts ~5m ago. They're currently affected. I’ve messaged both and queued status update.

ops-oncall: Rolling mitigation plan: 1) immediate: enable fallback throttles for non-enterprise tenants; 2) attempt manual provisioning for dedicated pool ; 3) enable model fallback to smaller quantized variants for non-SLA routes.

raj: Manual provisioning attempt failed due to provider quota. I’m opening a support ticket with the cloud provider now. ETA unknown.

sara: While provider fixes are unknown, we need in-cluster mitigations. Options: force-evict low-priority jobs, reduce per-request concurrency, enable soft-fallback to rwd-medium-6B for compatible routes. Thoughts?

eva: We have A/B mapping for a subset of routes that can tolerate lower-capacity models. I can flip a canary to route 20% of non-enterprise traffic to rwd-medium-6B. That will drop quality a bit but reduce GPU memory and allow throughput increase.

mike: I'll throttle token rate for anonymous/free-tier keys to 50% via rate-limit config: `PATCH /config/rate-limits {\"anonymous\": {\"token_rate\": 0.5}}`

julia: Please ensure we exclude enterprise tokens from throtte — they have SLAs.

raj: Provider support acknowledged ticket: INC-99871. They note short-term quota exhaustion, suggested we request temporary quota bump or move some capacity to another region.

sara: Fallback plan: (a) enable canary fallback (eva), (b) apply anonymous throttle (mike), (c) evict backlog of best-effort jobs older than 30m (raj/mike). Execute now.

mike: Applying anonymous throttle now. Patch response: 200 OK.

mike: Throttle in effect — anonymous QPS down ~48% within 60s.

eva: Starting canary flip for 20% of non-enterprise traffic to rwd-medium-6B. Will monitor quality/regressions and latency.

mike: Canary started. Observing immediate reduction in queue pressure: queue length dropped from 12k -> 8.7k in 3m. p95 latency down to 2.7s.

julia: Sent update to impacted customers: short-term throttling and fallback applied, engineers are actively mitigating. Asked to report if major regressions in output.

ops-oncall: Good. Next: schedule relocation of some burst traffic to eu-central-1 if provider can provide capacity. raj, can you check cross-region routing policy limits?

raj: Cross-region routing is enabled but requires warm pools in eu-central-1. We have some warm capacity there but not enough to absorb full surge. I can spin up extra warm pods but again provider quota is the blocker.

sara: For postmortem, capture: root cause = provider quota (scaleup-limit) + sudden traffic spike from rwd-large-16B workloads; mitigations: throttling, model fallback, evictions; customer impact: elevated 429/timeouts for enterprise for ~5-12m before mitigation.

mike: Adding quick commands/logs here for ops runbook:
```
# check autoscaler errors
kubectl -n infra logs deploy/autoscaler | grep scaleup
# queue snapshot
kubectl -n inference exec -it svc/queue-metrics -- curl /snapshot
```

raj: Provider ticket updates: they provisioned small temporary quota increase (10 GPUs) — will finish in ~9m.

mike: Observed additional capacity arrive at 2257890300. Autoscaler accepted nodes and started scheduling. Queue down to 2.1k now. p95 latency ~1.1s.

julia: Customers acknowledged update and saw improvements. No major data exposure; only degraded availability and increased latency.

sara: Good. Immediate actions summary: 
- throttled anonymous/free tier (mike)
- canary fallback to rwd-medium-6B for non-enterprise (eva)
- evicted best-effort backlog >30m (mike/raj)
- provider quota ticket opened and temporary quota granted (raj)

ops-oncall: Post-incident action items (assignments):
1) raj: follow up with provider for permanent quota bump or autoscale fallback to alternate region (due: 3d)
2) eva: create playbook for safe model fallback mappings + regression guardrails (due: 5d)
3) mike: add automated detection alert for provider-429/quota errors in autoscaler logs (due: 2d)
4) sara: run postmortem doc and RCA (due: 4d)

sara: I'll kick off a postmortem doc and include timestamps, graphs, and customer impact notes. Anyone with extra logs or traces drop them here and I'll attach.

raj: I’m pasting a snippet from provider support: `temporary quota granted until 2026-12-12T06:00:00Z; apply for formal increase via console`.

mike: Adding alert rule draft: `alert: AutoscalerProvider429Detected expr: rate(autoscaler_provider_errors_total{code=\"429\"}[1m]) > 0`

eva: Will prepare a regression evaluation harness for model fallbacks and add canary monitor to auto-rollback if output deviance > threshold.

julia: CS follow-ups: 1) proactive outreach to 5 affected customers with timeline; 2) provide post-incident summary once Sara publishes.

sara: Closing live handoff — monitoring for 30 more mins then will mark resolved. Thanks everyone. :heart:

incident-bot: Incident status: mitigated — queue pressure reduced, temporary provider quota provisioned. Keep thread for postmortem notes.

sara: Final note for postmortem: Recommend 1) quota monitoring + auto-fallback region, 2) pre-approved emergency provider quota request process, 3) rate-limit tiers and fallback model mappings reviewed and tested.

ops-oncall: Acknowledged. Will track action items in our incident tracker.
